Violation ID: 983710
Permit API: 117-22101
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/01/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's DCNR 587 02-003 well site located in Ward Township, Tioga County on 2/1/2023 at 1540 hours. The weather was 26 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in by Repsol.On 2/1/2023 at ~1335 hours, a release of ~5 barrels of produced water, ice and sand was discovered by Repsol after a line on a sand trap froze and split. Water, ice and sand was release to the pad surface near the wellheads onsite (photos #1 and 2). Sand, ice and dirt was recovered and placed in a 55-gallon drum for later disposal. The release mixed with onsite stormwater that was held in and around the well cellars. An onsite vacuum truck recovered a reported 1000 gallons of stormwater mixed with the produced water from the cellars and impacted area. I field measured all of the fluids in and around the impacted area for electrical conductivity utilizing an Oakton PCTS 50 meter. All readings ranged from 400 to 680us/cm today. Based on the reported release of ~5 barrels of produced water to the pad surface, new violations of the following are cited against API #117-22101 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.301Violations cited against API #117-22101 on 7/27/2022 remain outstanding at this time. I departed the site at 1615 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-11-24 to Range Resources Appalachia Llc in Amwell Twp, Washington county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Range Resources Appalachia Llc

Violation Date: 2019-11-24
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 869680
Permit API: 125-28720
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Amwell Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-11-24
Comments: On November 24, 2019, I conducted an inspection of the Kingston 11485 Well 5H well in Amwell Twp., Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of Oil Base Drill Mod (OBM) reported 11/23/2019 at 09:10pm. The Operator reported that approximately 3 barrels of OBM was discovered around the cellar in the process of excavating a production line trench near the well head. At the time of inspection, I spoke with Range Resources representatives Nate Smiell and John Fountain I observed a thick black material approximately 2 feet below the well pad furnace adjacent ot the 5H well (API 37-125-28720). A drill rig was not located on site. Mr. Smiell indicated that drilling was completed at the end of October 2019 and the well was in the process of being equipped for production prior to the stimulation of the well. The interior of the 5H well cellar was stained black. According to Mr. Smiell the black staining was part OBM and part spray adhesive residue from the installation of secondary containment. Additionally, after drilling was complete the secondary containment was removed. Mr. Smiell indicated that no observation of OBM or staining was made until the report on 11/23/2019. The reviewed the PPC and ER plan. I requested that the Operator add the Gator Sorb that was being utilized as part of the clear up process to the SDS sheets on site. I also requested an electronic copy of the Gator Sorb SDS sheets. I reviewed the E&S plan associated with the site. The key way drains were marked on the E&S plan. A Department WQS (BAM) approved reline changes to the E&S plan on 5/23/2019 and 7/8/2019. The key way drains appeared to be approved via red line change on 7/8/2019. I inspected the key way drains and sediment trap #2. No observation of sheen or OBM was made at any of the key way drains or sediment trap #2. It appears that the released material is localized to the well pad. I reviewed the E&S well pad grading plan, it appears that the lowest spot on the well pad is the ear near the 5H well. I recommend that the Operator continue with the remediation process and to monitor the key way drains and waters of the commonwealth for evidence that the release spread WOC. I was unbale to positively identify the sources of the released material. Violations are being issued related to the release of material to the ground surface and additional violation maybe forth coming based on the Departments investigation.

properties.content:

Violation Code: 78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks.
Violation ID: 956912
Permit API: 083-56364
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Lafayette Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/25/2022
Comments: This well was stimulated on 5/17/2022 and is currently being produced with a pump jack. The operator information is displayed on the pump jack. The pit used during the completion of this well has been reclaimed. Earth disturbance associated with reclaiming this pit and installing gathering lines alongside the spur road to the location has not been temporarily stabilized. A film of oil is evident on numerous trees along the southern edge of the location (beyond the pit). Stained soil with elevated specific conductivity (SPC) is also evident along various pathways across the forest floor downslope of where the pit was located. This is indicative that during the notching and/or frac'ing of this well, fluids associated with doing so were not sufficiently directed and/or contained in a pit. Two valves on the frac tank located at the southwestern corner of the well site are currently open and brine/production fluids are actively dripping out of them. Crude oil is pooled at both ends of the tank near the discharge points (valves) and the soil is stained for several feet downslope of each. SPC readings of the soil near the discharge points exceeded the upper limits of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Trees near the west side of the tank appear stressed as a result of the discharge from the tank. These observations are indicative that an appreciable (unknown) amount of brine/production fluids were released through the open valves on this tank. I contacted Justin Hansen of Bull Run and scheduled a field meeting to review these findings and discuss remediation options.

Inspection Date: 3/23/2023
Comments: On 3/23/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Mowry 1H-6H well site. It was 50 degrees and lightly raining when I arrived on location. When I arrived on site, I met with the Chesapeake Company man Danny Lambert who described current operations as follows: Nabors Drilling Rig X18 was on site, installing the production casing for the last of two new wells. The two existing wells have been shut in for the duration of the drilling and completion process. Crews were in the process of running the production casing and would be cementing it in later tonight. They are expected to start rigging down tomorrow. Danny said that they would be conducting a rig, drilling equipment, and secondary containment wash as they are removing equipment. Danny expects the rig to be off location by 3/31/2023.Danny accompanied me on the site inspection. The drilling rig and ancillary equipment are stationed on drilling mats within plastic lined secondary containment. The drill cuttings are collected, processed, temporarily stored and loaded for disposal; all actions conducted over secondary containment. I did witness two small areas of water/mud near the drill cuttings processing area that field tested at 2.43 mS and 2.44 mS conductance. Chemicals are stored on the northeast corner of the pad. Most were staged in secondary containment. Two totes were noted that overhung the containment edge. I discussed this with Danny who said they would be moved immediately. I did witness a 6 foot wide by 20 foot long erosional channel leaving the pad surface on the northeast corner. There were some pockets of water that would amount to less than two gallons in this erosional channel that field tested at 4.01 mS conductance or less. Soil in this channel field tested at less than 1.0 mS conductance. Soil down slope from the channel and in infiltration area 1 field tested at less than 1.0 mS conductance. Temporary stabilization had been applied to the eroded area.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. The fill slope on the northeast corner did have temporary stabilization. PCSM is addressed on site by two retentive grading/infiltration areas that were adequately stabilized and appeared to be functioning as designed. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3455915 for elevated conductance fluid detected on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations. The DEP recommends the following:1. Remove the elevated conductance fluid from the pad surface near the drill cuttings processing area.2. Assess the condition of the north east corner of the pad where the erosion or channel is forming and repair as necessary.3. Use good housekeeping practices when removing the drilling equipment and containments from location.I left the site at 1330 hrs.

Inspection Date: 2/08/2021
Comments: On 02/08/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone prepared an administrative report regarding Chesapeake Appalachia LLC's (CALLC) Stone BRA pad in Tuscarora Twp., Bradford County. The purpose of this report is to document CALLC's Notice of Violation (NOV) response for NOV 391862 and to upload the response to eFACTS. Details regarding the initial NOV issuance can be found within inspection report # 3141162. On 02/05/2021, CALLC issued their NOV response regarding NOV 391862 via electronic mail. CALLC stated their acknowledgment of violations of 35 P.S. 691.402(b) (Clean Streams Law), 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) (improper waste storage), and 35 P.S. 6018.301 (Solid Waste Management Act, improper waste storage) due to a produced water release on their Stone BRA pad. The released volume was estimated to be greater than one barrel (42 gallons). The release occurred on the Stone BRA pad, due to a breach in a produced water frac tank containment. CALLC's response identified produced fluids as being the regulated substance involved in the release, in the presence of precipitation. An area of approximately 37 feet by 42 feet by < 1 foot (depth) was delineated via soil conductivity field screening and scraped. 10 post-excavation samples were collected in accordance with systematic random sampling by Creston Environmental, LLC (Creston). Excavated soils were placed within containment, covered, and labeled, awaiting waste characterization for proper disposal. The cause of the containment breach was believed to be caused by a dropped connection hose. CALLC stated that the containment was repaired on 01/30/2021 by Creston. CALLC stated that the release remained isolated on the pad, did not reach or threaten any water supplies or surface waters, and did not impact any buildings or utilities. CALLC plans to document remedial action, associated attainment results, and restoration within an Act 2 deliverable. The information within CALLC's NOV response satisfies the 25 Pa. Code 78a.66c(2)(i). The NOV response has been uploaded to eFACTS with this report.

Comments: Site inspection conducted to review residual waste processing activity. Meeting on site today with STL Company Man Tim Fields. Weather at time of inspection is sunny and 80 degrees Fahrenheit.According to Mr. Fields, Precision Drilling Rig #110 has recently completed cementing the surface casing (depth 670') on the 1001H well (API #035-21329). The Blowout preventer is being nippled up and drilling is expected to resume on the intermediate casing later this evening. This is the second of three wells to be drilled and the rig has previously drilled the surface casing on the 1005H well. Two production wells are shut in during current drilling operations. The rig is drilling on water based mud, but the backyard is currently idle. STL submitted a Request for Alternative Waste Management Practices (OG71-A) application on 6/19/22. The Department approved the request on 6/22/22. The intent of the authorization for onsite drill cuttings processing is to remove the solid fraction from the liquid (drilling muds and fluids) so that drilling fluid can be reused concurrently for further drilling. For more information, refer to the Form A application regarding drill cuttings processing (EFACTS authorization #1400373).During this inspection, conductivity screenings were taken within rig secondary containment, production fluid containment, and GPU containment. Fluid within containment for the 1009H GPU is observed with conductivity reading of 3.8mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming all secondary containment features associated with production equipment. All containment structures are in good repair and are functioning as designed.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Inspection Date: 5/07/2026
Comments: I conducted a follow up inspection of this conventional well that had a release occur in November of 2025, when a steel gathering line had ruptured resulting in crude oil contaminating ditches and soil. Initially the remediation of the site was progressing. There had been no signs of product at the under flow dams, there was no viable oil in the ditches. In preperation of obtaining confirmatory soil samples to evaluate if the remediation was sufficient, it was discovered another leak had developed on a different section of the same line. This operator indicated they will replace all of the steel line for this well with plastic/poly line. This release was caught early and as of now, appears to be less than 1 bbl of lost product and has impacted a minimal amount of soil.Bull Run employees had a roll off dumpster en-route to remove the impacted soil. The ruptured line was sucked out with a vac truck and will be removed while running new poly line. Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 948072
Permit API: 083-49666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of an oil and gas leak in the vicinity of Chappel Fork near the road crossing of RT 321 (CTS #362745). At the time of the report to DEP, I spoke to the complainant and determined the location to begin searching. I contacted Pennhills Resources as they have wells in the immediate vicinity, and we agreed to meet on site to look. After beginning at Rt 321 we headed east until we found some oil collected in a low spot. It appears as though a line has burst with some gas pressure on the line, causing oil and gas to bubble to the surface. The oil then flowed south and into a low swale, where the majority of it collected. Some crude then flowed through into a channel formed by the collection of two spring runs, and toward the main branch of Chappel Fork. Oil was collecting behind ice pockets and in between leaves and dead vegetation for approximately 200 feet. A small amount of sheen was noted in Chappel Fork, but no free product. Approximately 15-20 barrels of oil was emitted from the line in total. Another small area nearer to the creek when following the line was noted to contain some basic sediment and paraffin at the surface and under a hemlock tree; it is uncertain if this is another leak site or simply product following the line. Pennhills immediately moved to contain the spill with booms in the back channel, and then brought a mini excavator to site to dig up the line and slow the leak. The 2" line was uncovered and a band placed on the line, which was broken on the bottom. It was determined that the old access past well 9A could be used to mobilize equipment and some brush was removed to make for better access. A vac truck was brought to site to collect any free product available, which was able to get a large amount on the first load. It was determined the evening of 3/15 that the line belonged to Pennhills, who will be continuing to clean up the oil and soil until clean. The operator built two underflow dams to contain any free product flowing down the channel with melting ice starting to give way. Followup inspection will be performed as necessary.

Inspection Date: 2019-05-29
Comments: I arrived at the site at 10:34 in response to a reported spill incident of an unknown volume of a fluid substance spilled to the pad surface, and into stormwater in a site perimeter ditch. The weather conditions are partly cloudy skies, breezy, warm and humid, with temperatures in the low to mid 70's. Representing the Department during the inspection in addition to myself include Ken Kennedy, Eric Miller, Cassidy Moyer and Eric Rooney. Marvin Schellie, consultant of BKV, is the company man at the site. Representing BKV is Tom Weller, Matt Knight and Dale Bennett. Representing the BKV consultant Apex Environmental is Shelly Bowen, and Jamie Moran. Kevin Brady of Whitetail Environmental, a BKV consultant, is also at the site. The current drilling depth on the Reynolds 2H well is (3,096) feet. Air drilling is in progress. The intermediate casing was cemented on 5/27/19 according to Mr. Schellie. Mr. Weller explained that inadvertently, a bypass valve for an overflow line was left open on the Iron Horse shale gas separator. Following waiting on cement (WOC), displacement fluid was being unloaded from the intermediate casing, and the existing separator tank was half full. When changed over and pressuring up to resume air drilling, air and some remaining displacement fluid was inadvertently discharged across the open top tank under pressure, and overflowed the tank and containment. Mr. Weller estimated that less than (1) barrel (42) gallons, was released off containment. Mr. Weller explained that the displaced water was recycled from previous air drilling operations, which may include the use of various lube products, and air foaming and defoaming products. Mr. Brady provided the Department with Safety Data Sheets (SDS) of the products. The SDS indicates the chemical name for the lube product is ECO Drill 100, with biodegradable drill oil listed as a synonym. The SDS indicates the foaming product is FoamFresh, with Eco-Friendly Foamer listed as a synonym. Mr. Brady also provided the Department with photos of the source of the fluid spilled out of the container, the ditch which is labeled stormwater channel, and a map of the site. The container is located on secondary containment in the area on the pad surface termed the backyard by BKV. This particular area is located adjacent to the drilling rig and site perimeter berm. Mr. Brady informed the Department that he recorded specific conductance (conductivity) of (4) millisiemens/cm in water in the stormwater channel on 5/28/19 at 15:35, (145) parts per million in chlorides on a Hach test strip on 5/28/19 at 15:35, and a sump was constructed in the channel as a result of the elevated readings. He further stated that an on-site vacuum truck was immediately deployed to the area where the spill occurred, and an additional vacuum truck was dispatched to remove impacted stormwater in the channel. Apex informed the Department they screened the impacted area on the ground surface with a photoionization detector (PID) meter for the potential presence of volatile organic compounds at 8:24 AM today, 5/29/19, and screened the water in the channel for conductivity at 8:40 AM today, 5/29/19. Apex indicated they excavated small holes in (3) locations on the berm where the impact occurred, to obtain PID readings. The reading at the first location was (1.9) ppm; the second location was (1.6) ppm, and the third location was 1.5 ppm. The PID meter read (0) parts per million on containment near the tank as part of the release. Conductivity was (306) microsiemens/cm. I used a Hanna HI 98331 Groline Soil Test meter, and an Oakton PCTS 50 meter to record conductivity of water in the channel. During the inspection, the Department and Apex collected samples of stormwater in the channel in (3) separate locations. The Department also collected a sample of fluid in the container associated with the spill. See photos. The Department left the site at 13:28.

Inspection Date: 1/13/2025
Comments: On January 13, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of EQT's Herriott Well Pad after a spill was reported to the emergency hotline at 1:50pm on January 12, 2025. According to the spill report and a verbal conversation with Logan Dominick of EQT via the phone, at 1pm on 1/12/2025, a truck drove over a hose breaking the coupling on the hose releasing production fluids. Mr. Dominick stated that 90% of the spill occurred on containment and approximately 10% spilled off of containment. Mr. Dominick estimated that 10 gallons spilled and stated that SPSI scraped approximately 6 inches of the well pad in the spill area as well as vacuumed up the containment and placed all contaminated materials into a dumpster on site.At the time of this inspection EQT representative Jeremy Barber was on site and inform the Department that Flowback was currently occurring. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a section of the pad that was scrapped adjacent to two frack tanks that were in containment. The Department also observed a dumpster adjacent to the spill area. In the middle of the spill area appeared to be a strip of containment that had hoses in it. Mr. Barber pointed out that the open hose was the one that was ran over and caused the spill. The Department did not observe any holes or tears in the hose containment or the frack tank containment and the containments appeared to be dry.Background conductivity readings were taken adjacent to the well pad on the perimeter and some vegetation (0.289mS) and then readings were taken in the spill area that was scraped (0.0945 mS, 0.0386, 0.0416mS), then a reading was taken outside but directly adjacent to the spill area (0.0036 mS). Mr. Barber informed the Department that the area underneath these containments had not been scraped yet and that as soon as Flowback is completed, they will be pulled, the area beneath them will be scraped, and any contaminated material will be properly disposed of. The Department took conductivity readings at the edge/underneath this containment to determine if this area is contaminated, and the readings are as follows: 3.34 mS and 1.649 under/adjacent to the containment of the frack tanks where the spill occurred, and 13.98 mS under/adjacent to the containment where the hose is and where the spill originated. The soil conductivity readings in the spill area where the ground has been scraped, is comparable to the background reading and therefore appears to be remediated in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills, however, the readings in the area at the edge of/underneath the containment lining were elevated compared to the background reading and therefore appears to still be contaminated. The Department verbally recommended to Mr. Barber that the containment be lifted and materials be scraped as soon as possible. Mr. Barber informed The Department that SPSI will be back on site today and they will continue to remediate the release in accordance with policies. Mr. Barber also stated that photo documentation of continued remediate efforts will be supplied to the Department as soon as it is available. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection and the spill not being completely remediated yet, violations are being issued for an approximately 10 gallon release of production fluid from a hose onto the well pad.

The Department took conductivity readings at the edge/underneath this containment to determine if this area is contaminated, and the readings are as follows: 3.34 mS and 1.649 under/adjacent to the containment of the frack tanks where the spill occurred, and 13.98 mS under/adjacent to the containment where the hose is and where the spill originated. The soil conductivity readings in the spill area where the ground has been scraped, is comparable to the background reading and therefore appears to be remediated in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills, however, the readings in the area at the edge of/underneath the containment lining were elevated compared to the background reading and therefore appears to still be contaminated. The Department verbally recommended to Mr. Barber that the containment be lifted and materials be scraped as soon as possible. Mr. Barber informed The Department that SPSI will be back on site today and they will continue to remediate the release in accordance with policies. Mr. Barber also stated that photo documentation of continued remediate efforts will be supplied to the Department as soon as it is available. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection and the spill not being completely remediated yet, violations are being issued for an approximately 10 gallon release of production fluid from a hose onto the well pad.

The EC of the fluid in the sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel has an EC of 1645 uS/cm.Along the access road, vegetation has germinated where excavation took place after a truck rollover caused a release of produced fluid to an area surrounding the access road. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 1/27/2025
Violation Code: 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
Violation ID: 8214923
Permit API: 125-28510
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: East Finley Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/27/2025
Comments: On 12/27/2024 an Incident Response inspection was conducted the MOR42 Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/27/2024 CNX Resources Representative, Ben Geary, reported an approximately 40-gallon brine release off containment at the MOR42 Well Pad located in East Finley Township, Washington County.CNX Resources representative, Ben Geary, and SPSI representative, Mac Maydak, were on site at time of inspection. Mr. Geary informed the Department that that the release was discovered on Saturday, January 25 at 1:15 pm, that the quantity released was approximately 40 gallons, and that a contractor (SPSI) had been dispatched the same day. Mr. Maydak stated that his crew was dispatched on Saturday (1/25) at approximately 1:40 pm. The origin of the release was stated to be a crack found on a T-joint along a line connecting to a slug catcher to the production tanks, which could be observed in front of the Unit H Gas Processing Unit (GPU).Mr. Geary stated that remediation efforts had taken place Saturday (1/25), Sunday (1/26), and continued into today (1/27). The area remediated at the time of inspection measured approximately 38 by 18 feet and to a depth of 1 inch, excluding the sump created on the western side of the GPU that measured approximately 8 inches in depth. It was made known that field screening was conducted during the remediation efforts with screening values between 2,000 and 12,000 s/cm observed. Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 3/19/2026
Comments: On March 19, 2026, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, 4157162, 4157480, and 4157532. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports and discusses 8 observed culverts along the access road as well as any observed erosion and sedimentation issues along the access road. This Inspection Report is Inspection 1 of 2 and assesses Culverts 1-5. All associated violations discussed in both inspection reports are being issued/continued in just this inspection.A COA with the DEP was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, a rig was on site and plugging operations have commenced.During IRs 4157087/4157136/4157162, the DEP recommended the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan and redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.During IRs 4157480/4157532, the DEP recommended the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan. The DEP recommended the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5. The DEP recommended the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.At the time of this inspection, the E and S plan was present in the on-site mailbox at the beginning of the access road. The DEP did not observed any redlining on site plans to depict and appropriately match on-site field changes (Photo 2). The DEP also did not observe the RCE to be installed at the beginning of the access road as depicted on the plans (Photo 1). The access road was also observed to still not be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plan calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary". CFS was observed to be installed at an area where erosion and sedimentation off the access road was previously noted to be located before culvert 1.Observations obtained during today's inspection at culvert crossings 1-5 are as follows:Culvert 1 crossing - culverted for a roadside ditch (Photos 4-7): The outlet still appears to be block. CFS was observed at both the inlet and outlet, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete surface contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert 2 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 8-9): Outlet still appears to be blocked. CFS was observed to be installed and functioning properly at both the inlet and outlet. Culvert 3 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 10-13): The inlet to this culvert appears to still be blocked. CFS was installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.Culvert 4 crossing - culverted for roadside ditch (Photos 14-17): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert still appears to not be receiving water due to operator disturbing channel and causing water to be diverted further down access road. The disturbed channel still appears to be carrying fine sediment towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen (Photos 18-20).Culvert 5 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 21-24): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this crossing, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/08/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 907422
Permit API: 015-23632
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2/08/2021
Comments: On 02/08/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone prepared an administrative report regarding Chesapeake Appalachia LLC's (CALLC) Stone BRA pad in Tuscarora Twp., Bradford County. The purpose of this report is to document CALLC's Notice of Violation (NOV) response for NOV 391862 and to upload the response to eFACTS. Details regarding the initial NOV issuance can be found within inspection report # 3141162. On 02/05/2021, CALLC issued their NOV response regarding NOV 391862 via electronic mail. CALLC stated their acknowledgment of violations of 35 P.S. 691.402(b) (Clean Streams Law), 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) (improper waste storage), and 35 P.S. 6018.301 (Solid Waste Management Act, improper waste storage) due to a produced water release on their Stone BRA pad. The released volume was estimated to be greater than one barrel (42 gallons). The release occurred on the Stone BRA pad, due to a breach in a produced water frac tank containment. CALLC's response identified produced fluids as being the regulated substance involved in the release, in the presence of precipitation. An area of approximately 37 feet by 42 feet by < 1 foot (depth) was delineated via soil conductivity field screening and scraped. 10 post-excavation samples were collected in accordance with systematic random sampling by Creston Environmental, LLC (Creston). Excavated soils were placed within containment, covered, and labeled, awaiting waste characterization for proper disposal. The cause of the containment breach was believed to be caused by a dropped connection hose. CALLC stated that the containment was repaired on 01/30/2021 by Creston. CALLC stated that the release remained isolated on the pad, did not reach or threaten any water supplies or surface waters, and did not impact any buildings or utilities. CALLC plans to document remedial action, associated attainment results, and restoration within an Act 2 deliverable. The information within CALLC's NOV response satisfies the 25 Pa. Code 78a.66c(2)(i). The NOV response has been uploaded to eFACTS with this report.
